TITLE: Non-asymptotic sample complexity of KernelSHAP
PROPOSAL: We provide a non-asymptotic analysis of the sample complexity of KernelSHAP by showing that its strategy can be cast as an importance-weighted estimator, and then leverage uniform convergence results from importance-weighted averages to obtain a finite-sample convergence rate. Specifically, we show that with $n = O(d/\epsilon^2)$ samples, the L2 error of the estimated Shapley values is bounded by $\epsilon$, with high probability. This provides the first non-asymptotic guarantee for KernelSHAP.
CONTROLS: We compare against the known asymptotic regime and analyze the effect of different sampling distributions on the sample complexity.
COST: 6048000
PREDICTION: Our result provides a sharp finite-sample analysis of KernelSHAP, up to constants and logarithmic factors, and reveals how the choice of sampling distribution impacts its sample efficiency, with a gap between the best and worst distributions of a factor of up to d. The result is expected to hold only for distributions with weights in a certain range relative to the marginal probability of each subset.

TITLE: LeverageSHAP meets correspondence analysis
PROPOSAL: We develop a new estimator, dubbed CorrespondenceSHAP, which integrates LeverageSHAP with correspondence analysis, a dimensionality reduction technique. By leveraging the high-dimensional structure of the Shapley value equations, CorrespondenceSHAP efficiently approximates the Shapley values while maintaining the strong non-asymptotic theoretical guarantees of LeverageSHAP. Specifically, we demonstrate that CorrespondenceSHAP achieves the same convergence rate as LeverageSHAP, while reducing the computational cost by up to a factor of d.
CONTROLS: We compare against LeverageSHAP and KernelSHAP on various datasets, analyzing the impact of dimensionality on each estimator's performance.
COST: 25920000
PREDICTION: CorrespondenceSHAP is expected to outperform LeverageSHAP for very high-dimensional data, but may suffer from reduced accuracy when the number of features is small. Its performance on real-world datasets will be critical to assess its practical utility.

TITLE: A scalable and unbiased variant of Shapley values
PROPOSAL: We introduce a novel unbiased estimator of Shapley values, dubbed StratifiedSHAP, which uses stratified sampling to ef ciently approximate the expected contributions of individual features. By controlling the sampling distribution, StratifiedSHAP achieves strong asymptotic and non-asymptotic guarantees, including mean squared error bounds and variance guarantees. Furthermore, we show that StratifiedSHAP can be computationally optimized using optimization techniques, resulting in a fast and scalable method for computing Shapley values in high-dimensional settings.
CONTROLS: We compare against KernelSHAP, LeverageSHAP, and CorrespondenceSHAP, investigating their performance under stratified sampling.
COST: 77760000
PREDICTION: StratifiedSHAP is expected to achieve the best balance between bias and variance among existing methods, providing an efficient and highly accurate estimate of Shapley values, particularly in high-dimensional settings. Its effectiveness will depend on finding an optimal tradeoff between the number of strata and the number of samples.

TITLE: Investigating the effect of kernel choice on KernelSHAP
PROPOSAL: We conduct an in-depth analysis of the impact of kernel choice on the performance of KernelSHAP, including its accuracy, stability, and computational cost. We compare various widely-used kernels and propose a novel adaptive kernel selection strategy, which automatically selects the optimal kernel based on the given data and features. Additionally, we investigate the role of kernel alignment in the convergence rate of KernelSHAP and derive theoretical bounds on the kernel's influence on the estimator's performance.
CONTROLS: We extensively evaluate KernelSHAP with different kernels on several real-world datasets and assess its sensitivity to kernel misalignment.
COST: 108000000
PREDICTION: Our results will provide a deeper understanding of the relationship between kernel choice and KernelSHAP's performance, highlighting the importance of carefully selecting a suitable kernel for the task at hand. The optimal kernel may depend on the specific problem and data characteristics, but a well-designed adaptive strategy can automate kernel selection to some extent.

TITLE: Shapley values for high-dimensional neural networks
PROPOSAL: We introduce a novel method for approximating Shapley values in high-dimensional neural networks by leveraging the information encoded in the neural network's weights and activations. We develop a neural network-based approach that uses a specially designed neural network to approximate the Shapley values, which we call SHAP-NETS. We demonstrate the effectiveness of SHAP-NETS on various high-dimensional datasets and show that it achieves superior performance compared to existing methods for approximating Shapley values.
CONTROLS: We compare SHAP-NETS against StratifiedSHAP and other state-of-the-art methods to evaluate its effectiveness and efficiency.
COST: 2430000 
PREDICTION: SHAP-NETS is expected to provide a high-fidelity approximation of Shapley values in high-dimensional neural networks, achieving significant improvements over existing methods in terms of accuracy, efficiency, and interpretability, but it might require large amount of computations and memory.

TITLE: A computational framework for scalable Shapley value estimation
PROPOSAL: We develop a computational framework for scalable Shapley value estimation by incorporating several state-of-the-art methods, including StratifiedSHAP, SHAP-NETS, and CorrespondenceSHAP, into a unified framework that allows for easy comparison and combination of these methods. We provide a software implementation of the framework, which we call SHAP-Framework, and demonstrate its effectiveness on various high-dimensional datasets.
CONTROLS: We evaluate the performance of SHAP-Framework on several real-world datasets and compare its results against the individual methods included in the framework.
COST: 2592000000
PREDICTION: SHAP-Framework is expected to provide a flexible and scalable platform for Shapley value estimation, achieving significant improvements over individual methods in terms of accuracy, efficiency, and interpretability, but might require significant computational resources.

TITLE: Theoretical limitations of Shapley value estimation
PROPOSAL: We provide a theoretical analysis of the limitations of Shapley value estimation, highlighting the intrinsic trade-offs between accuracy, efficiency, and interpretability. We derive information-theoretic lower bounds on the convergence rate and sample complexity of Shapley value estimation, showing that some optimal trade-offs are fundamental limitations. We also demonstrate that these lower bounds are tight for several popular methods, including StratifiedSHAP and SHAP-NETS.
CONTROLS: We compare our theoretical results against the empirical performance of popular Shapley value estimators to assess their practical relevance.
COST: 485000000000 
PREDICTION: Our results are expected to provide a deeper understanding of the fundamental limitations of Shapley value estimation, highlighting the intrinsic trade-offs between accuracy, efficiency, and interpretability, and providing a benchmark for future methods to improve upon.

TITLE: Improving Shapley value estimation with active learning
PROPOSAL: We integrate active learning into Shapley value estimation to improve accuracy and efficiency. We propose an active learning algorithm that selects the most informative samples to query, and use these samples to improve the Shapley value estimates. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our algorithm on various high-dimensional datasets, and show that it achieves significant improvements over passive learning methods.
CONTROLS: We compare our active learning algorithm against stratified sampling and other active learning methods to evaluate its effectiveness.
COST: 32256000000
PREDICTION: Our active learning algorithm is expected to improve the accuracy and efficiency of Shapley value estimation, particularly in high-dimensional settings where passive learning methods may struggle, but may require significant computational resources for optimal performance.

TITLE: A unified framework for explainability and uncertainty quantification
PROPOSAL: We propose a unified framework that integrates Shapley value estimation and uncertainty quantification for machine learning models. We introduce a new methodology that combines Shapley values with predictive uncertainty to provide a more comprehensive understanding of model behavior. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our framework on various high-dimensional datasets and show that it improves the interpretability and reliability of machine learning models.
CONTROLS: We compare our unified framework against existing methods for explainability and uncertainty quantification to evaluate its effectiveness.
COST: 622500000000
PREDICTION: Our unified framework is expected to provide a comprehensive understanding of model behavior, integrating the strengths of Shapley value estimation and uncertainty quantification to improve the interpretability and reliability of machine learning models, but it might require significant computational resources and expert knowledge in both explainability and Bayesian modeling.

TITLE: Long-Term Temporal Change Description with Temporally-Constrained MLLMs
PROPOSAL: Fine-tune the multimodal large language model (MM-LM) BERT-LMADA+va  to perform change description on the Terra-i dataset (Hoseini et al., 2020), conditioning on all previous images in the sequence to reason about long-term trends, and incorporating temporal information as an additional input token sequence to capture temporal relationships between events.
CONTROLS: Baseline performance of MM-LM on Terra-i without temporal conditioning, second-order Markov Random Fields with scene graph based temporal reasoning, and Temporal Transformer for time-series analysis
COST: 900 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The temporally-constrained MLLM can be shown to significantly outperform existing methods on change description with a unique blend of past and future context, most notably in describing complex patterns involving disparate phases of change (e.g. crop rotation) with harmonic evolution over time.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Memory-Augmented Temporal Consistency for Satellite Image Forecasting
PROPOSAL: Modify the diffusion-based image synthesizer, DALL-E 2-MV-SAT, to incorporate an attention-based memory mechanism that selectively retains and updates memories of historical changes, allowing the model to maintain long-term consistency with observed trends while predicting future changes.
CONTROLS: Baseline performance of DALL-E 2-MV-SAT on satellite image forecasting, adding a fixed window of historical images as input, and a Temporal Convolutional Network (TCN) with a fixed number of layers for temporal reasoning
COST: 1200 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The memory-augmented DALL-E 2-MV-SAT can generate temporally consistent forecasts, showcasing improved performance on land-use change prediction tasks where long-term trends are critical, but may falter in spontaneous or uncertain events where established patterns break down.

TITLE: Forecasting Future Scenes from Irregularly-Sampled Satellite Time Series
PROPOSAL: Develop an irregularly-sampled temporal modeling architecture, utilizing aσεις blockchain domain temporal decoding layer within a temporal graph convolutional network (TGCN), to learn to predict future satellite images given an uneven sequence of observations, while incorporating prior knowledge about the timescales of change in different domains (e.g., agricultural, urban).
CONTROLS: Baseline performance of uniform sampling-based forecasting methods, a equidistant sampling approach using periodic forecasting deep Unfolding Recurrent Neural Networks for regression (URNR-N), and a traditional TGCN with fixed learning rate for sampling frequency
COST: 1500 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The new architecture will effectively learn to reason about the temporal effects of sampling in addition to the inherent properties of scene change allowing it to generalize to and accurately predict the changes observed from satellite images acquired at non-uniform sampling rates.

ACTION: REVISE 1
TITLE: Long-Term Temporal Change Description with Temporally-Constrained MLLMs
PROPOSAL: Revise the fine-tuning procedure for the temporally-constrained MLLM (BERT-LMADA+va) to also utilize an entropy-based sample weighting scheme to dynamically adjust the influence of images in the sequence, giving more weight to images corresponding to periods of high change or uncertainty.
CONTROLS: Baseline performance of fine-tuning without entropy-based weighting, a uniform weighting scheme, and a separate entropy-based model for sequence classification
COST: 1350 GPU-hours (increased due to the need to re-train the weighting mechanism)
PREDICTION: The revised MLLM can better focus its attention on the most informative points in the temporal sequence, which should enhance its ability to accurately describe complex patterns of change and capture the uncertainties associated with prediction when domain knowledge or uncertainty in past observations are factored in.

TITLE: Evaluating Temporal Consistency with Learned Metrics
PROPOSAL: Train an adversarial critic model to evaluate the temporal consistency of satellite image forecasts generated by existing models (including the memory-augmented DALL-E 2-MV-SAT and the irreps ending up proposed in future turns). This learned metric can be used to quantify the consistency of forecasts in addition to existing metrics such as visual similarity or temporal coherence.
CONTROLS: Baseline performance of existing methods on consistency evaluation, a simple multi-step temporal forecasting approach with the existing consistency metrics, and a sequence of walks on a graph for a Markov distribution over the time-dependent image patterns
COST: 1500 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The learned metric will capture richer temporal semantic relationships between consecutive forecasted images than existing evaluation methods, leading to more informative and detailed comparisons of the quality and consistency of satellite image forecasts, most profitably in efficiency improvement of human-challenge.

ACTION: REVISE 4
TITLE: Evaluating Temporal Consistency with Learned Metrics
PROPOSAL: Enhance the trained adversarial critic model to also assess changes in the underlying probability distribution of forecasts over time, by incorporating a temporal latent variable that learns to capture the evolving dynamics of the scene; this capability will enable more comprehensive evaluation of models' ability to reason about temporal semantics.
CONTROLS: Baseline performance of the critic model without temporal capability, a simpler temporal forecasting approach with grid-based temporal auto-correlation analysis, and a sequence of previous yet adjacent consecutive images that running videos with no vast rotations or flips exist at multiple CCTV sites
COST: 2100 GPU-hours (increased due to the need to incorporate the additional latent variable)
PREDICTION: The revised learned metric will effectively quantify the temporal plausibility and semantic coherence of forecasts, enabling a more nuanced assessment of models' ability to reason about long-term dynamics and change over time.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Joint Learning of Temporal Change Description and Forecasting
PROPOSAL: Explore a unified architecture that jointly learns to describe and forecast changes in satellite image time series, by formulating change description and forecasting as a single optimization problem with shared temporal semantic reasoning, using the temporally-constrained MLLM and the memory-augmented DALL-E 2-MV-SAT as components.
CONTROLS: Baseline performance of separate models for change description and forecasting, a conditional random field that combines probability of change and probability of continuation separately under given conditions along time series, and a stack-based ensemble with contextual sentential parallelization
COST: 3600 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The joint learning approach can leverage the strengths of both change description and forecasting, leading to improved performance on both tasks, and can capture complex temporal relationships between changes and forecasts by sharing semantic reasoning across them.

ACTION: REVISE 5
TITLE: Joint Learning of Temporal Change Description and Forecasting
PROPOSAL: Incorporate the learned metric from proposal 4 into the joint learning architecture, so that the unified model also learns to reason about the temporal consistency of its forecasts during training, by incorporating a loss term that encourages the forecasts to be consistent with the timeline of past changes.
CONTROLS: Baseline performance of joint learning without the learned metric, a learning-to-rank approach using the learned metric as a ranking signal, and a temporal segment networking combination using both earlier models
COST: 4500 GPU-hours (increased due to the need to incorporate the additional loss term)
PREDICTION: The revised joint learning model can effectively optimize for both accurate change description and temporally consistent forecasting, leading to improved performance on both tasks and more reliable predictions of future changes.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Learning to Automate Temporal Abstractions for Satellite Change Analysis
PROPOSAL: Develop a model to learn to identify and represent temporal abstractions (e.g., seasons,(event) holidays) from the satellite image time series data, and then incorporate these abstractions into the joint learning architecture to enable more effective reasoning about long-term temporal changes and consistency.
CONTROLS: Baseline performance of manual temporal abstraction, a rule-based system for temporal abstraction with predefined rules and limited domain knowledge, and a separate clustering-based approach to identify temporal patterns
COST: 7500 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The learned temporal abstractions will enable the joint learning model to capture and reason about high-level temporal patterns and relationships, leading to improved performance on both change description and forecasting tasks, most notably in capturing complex seasonal or periodic patterns in satellite image time series.

ACTION: REVISE 3
TITLE: Forecasting Future Scenes from Irregularly-Sampled Satellite Time Series
PROPOSAL: Enhance the irregularly-sampled temporal modeling architecture to also incorporate the learned temporal abstractions from proposal 6, so that it can reason about high-level temporal patterns and relationships in addition to the observed changes and timescales, leading to improved performance on forecasting tasks with complex temporal dynamics.
CONTROLS: Baseline performance of forecasting without temporal abstractions, a temporal tree model with static potential locations for abstractions, and a spacetime-gridded Markov network for capture ambient supertemporal influence using posterior separation
COST: 8400 GPU-hours (increased due to the need to incorporate the learned temporal abstractions)
PREDICTION: The revised forecasting model can capture and reason about both low-level changes and high-level temporal patterns, leading to more accurate and reliable predictions of future satellite images, even in the presence of complex and irregular temporal dynamics.

ACTION: ADD 1
TITLE:  Investigating Adapter Parameters for Online Traffic Flow Forecasting
PROPOSAL: We will extend the popular MoWoE (Multi-Output Wide & Ensemble) model used for traffic flow forecasting by adding two adapters: one linear and one non-linear. We will, a) pre-train MoWoE on a traffic dataset (e.g., METR-LA) and observe its performance on unseen data, b) update only the parameters of the linear and non-linear adapters using a mixture of experience replay and online gradient descent while freezing MoWoE's weights, and c) compare the forecasting performance of the adapted model with the baseline, where the entire MoWoE is re-trained on the available past data at each time step using online gradient descent.
CONTROLS: Baseline updates of the entire MoWoE model using online gradient descent based on one time step, and an ablation study where only the linear adapter is updated or only the non-linear adapter is updated.
COST: 3000
PREDICTION: We expect that updating both adapters will lead to the best forecasting performance compared to updating the entire MoWoE model or only one adapter, especially in cases of rapid concept drift due to the reduced number of parameters being updated.

ACTION: ADD 2
TITLE:  Analyzing Gradient Delay in Multi-Step Forecasting
PROPOSAL: We will investigate the impact of delayed feedback on multi-step forecasting using a 2D convolutional neural network (2DCNN) architecture. We will a) train 2DCNN on an electricity consumption forecasting dataset (e.g., ENB) to make 24-step ahead forecasts, b) simulate delayed feedback scenarios where the true values for forecasts made at time t are not available until time t+24, and c) evaluate the forecasting performance of 2DCNN under different feedback delay settings.
CONTROLS: A baseline where the true values are immediately available after each prediction and ablation studies on the architecture complexity of 2DCNN (e.g., different numbers of layers or filters), as reducing the model capacity may mitigate the impact of delayed feedback.
COST: 5000
PREDICTION: We expect that the forecasting performance will degrade as the feedback delay increases, with significant drops in performance for delays exceeding 6 steps, and we hypothesize that reducing the model capacity may alleviate the issue by reducing the variance of the gradient estimates.

ACTION: REVISE 1
TITLE:  Investigating Adapter Parameters for Online Traffic Flow Forecasting with Dynamic Adapters
PROPOSAL: We extend Proposal 1 by introducing dynamic adapters: at each time step, the architecture and parameters of the adapters are updated based on the new data and the forecasting error. We will a) pre-train MoWoE on a traffic dataset (e.g., METR-LA), b) learning the adapter architecture and parameters at each time step using a mixture of experience replay and online gradient descent, and c) evaluate the performance of the adapted model on unseen data.
CONTROLS: The original baseline ( Proposal 1(a) ) and an ablation study where the adapter architecture remains fixed.
COST: 4500
PREDICTION: We expect that dynamic adapters will lead to improved forecasting performance on rapidly changing data, as they can adapt to changing patterns in real-time, and this improvement will be substantial when compared to the fixed adapters setup (Proposal 1).

ACTION: ADD 3
TITLE:  Investigating Covariate Shift Detection for Online Concept Drift
PROPOSAL: We propose a novel approach to detect covariate shift in online time series forecasting, based on a statistical test for the change in mean and variance of input features. We will a) collect input features from a traffic flow dataset (e.g., METR-LA) over time, b) train a statistical model to detect changes in the distribution of these features, and c) trigger updates of the forecasting model (e.g., MoWoE) only when significant changes are detected.
CONTROLS: A baseline where the forecasting model is updated at regular time intervals and an ablation study where the detection model is replaced with a simpler change-point detection algorithm.
COST: 5400
PREDICTION: We expect that the proposed approach will detect covariate shift accurately and significantly reduce the number of unnecessary model updates, thereby improving forecasting performance and reducing computation costs.

ACTION: REVISE 2
TITLE:  Analyzing Gradient Delay in Multi-Step Forecasting with Successive Approximation Method
PROPOSAL: We extend Proposal 2 by incorporating the successive approximation method, which uses an iterative procedure to refine the forecast and reduce the impact of delayed feedback. We will a) train a 2D convolutional neural network (2DCNN) on an electricity consumption forecasting dataset (e.g., ENB) to make 24-step ahead forecasts, b) simulate delayed feedback scenarios where the true values for forecasts made at time t are not available until time t+24, and c) evaluate the forecasting performance of 2DCNN under different feedback delay settings using the successive approximation method with various number of iterations.
CONTROLS: The original baseline ( Proposal 2 ) and an ablation study where the successive approximation method is replaced with a simpler heuristic for mitigating delayed feedback (e.g., using an exponential moving average of past errors).
COST: 9000
PREDICTION: We expect that the successive approximation method will significantly improve forecasting performance under delayed feedback scenarios, especially when combined with an appropriate number of iterations, and this improvement will be substantial compared to the baseline and other heuristics.

ACTION: ADD 4
TITLE:  Multi-Task Learning for Online Forecasting of Multiple Time Series
PROPOSAL: We investigate the application of multi-task learning to online forecasting of multiple time series. We will a) collect datasets for traffic flow, electricity consumption, and other time series forecasting tasks, b) train a single neural network model to learn shared features across tasks, and c) evaluate the performance of the multi-task model on each individual task.
CONTROLS: Baselines where separate models are trained for each task and an ablation study where the shared feature learning component is removed, allowing each task to learn its own features.
COST: 7500
PREDICTION: We expect that the multi-task model will improve forecasting performance on each individual task, especially for tasks with similar underlying patterns, and this improvement will be more significant when the tasks have strong correlations or share similar characteristics.

ACTION: REVISE 3
TITLE:  Investigating Covariate Shift Detection for Online Concept Drift with Attention Mechanism
PROPOSAL: We extend Proposal 3 by incorporating an attention mechanism to focus on the most relevant input features when detecting covariate shift. We will a) collect input features from a traffic flow dataset (e.g., METR-LA) over time, b) train an attention-based statistical model to detect changes in the distribution of these features, and c) trigger updates of the forecasting model (e.g., MoWoE) only when significant changes are detected.
CONTROLS: The original baseline ( Proposal 3 ) and an ablation study where the attention mechanism is replaced with a simpler feature selection method (e.g., correlation-based feature selection).
COST: 8400
PREDICTION: We expect that the attention-based model will improve covariate shift detection by focusing on the most relevant features and reduce the number of unnecessary model updates, thereby improving forecasting performance and reducing computation costs.

ACTION: ADD 5
TITLE:  Robust Online Forecasting under Concept Drift with Gaussian Process
PROPOSAL: We investigate the application of Gaussian Processes for robust online forecasting under concept drift. We will a) train a Gaussian Process model on a traffic flow dataset (e.g., METR-LA) to learn a probabilistic distribution over possible forecasts, b) update the model online using a streaming algorithm to adapt to changes in the data distribution, and c) evaluate the performance of the Gaussian Process model in comparison to other online forecasting methods.
CONTROLS: Baselines where a single Gaussian Process model is trained offline and where an online version of a traditional machine learning algorithm (e.g., neural network) is used.
COST: 11400
PREDICTION: We expect that the Gaussian Process model will provide robust online forecasting performance under concept drift, capturing uncertainties in the forecasting process and adapting quickly to changes in the data distribution.

ACTION: REVISE 4
TITLE:  Multi-Task Learning for Online Forecasting of Multiple Time Series with Transfer Learning
PROPOSAL: We extend Proposal 4 by incorporating transfer learning to adapt the shared features learned across tasks to a new task with a different data distribution. We will a) collect datasets for traffic flow, electricity consumption, and other time series forecasting tasks, b) train a single neural network model to learn shared features across tasks using transfer learning, and c) evaluate the performance of the multi-task model on each individual task, including the new task.
CONTROLS: The original baseline ( Proposal 4 ) and an ablation study where the transfer learning component is removed, and the model is trained from scratch on the new task.
COST: 10500
PREDICTION: We expect that the transfer learning will improve the adaptability of the multi-task model to new tasks with different data distributions, and this improvement will be substantial compared to the baseline and other adaptation methods (e.g., fine-tuning a pre-trained model).

ACTION: ADD 6
TITLE:  A Unified Framework for Online Time Series Forecasting under Concept Drift
PROPOSAL: We propose a unified framework for online time series forecasting under concept drift, which integrates benchmark algorithms and novel techniques for addressing the two core challenges of online time series learning: which parameters to update and how to update them. We will a) implement a comprehensive evaluation framework to compare the performance of different online time series forecasting methods under various concept drift scenarios, and b) evaluate the performance of our unified framework on a range of real-world time series datasets.
CONTROLS: Baselines where individual methods are used for updating and adapting to concept drift, and ablation studies where components of the unified framework are removed or replaced.
COST: 18000
PREDICTION: We expect that the unified framework will provide a robust and adaptive solution for online time series forecasting under concept drift, outperforming individual methods and providing a flexible platform for incorporating novel techniques and applications.

ACTION: ADD 1
TITLE: Heterogeneous Retrieval Aggregation
PROPOSAL: Compare three aggregation methods (element-wise addition, fusion with neural attention, late interaction) for combining dense text and vision-centric multimodal embeddings: a) element-wise addition, where query and document embeddings are aligned by dimensionality and then added; b) fusion with neural attention, where attention weights are learned to select the most relevant features; and c) late interaction, where the two embeddings are transformed through parallel neural networks before being combined.
CONTROLS: Baseline multimodal retriever (ColPali-based encoder), ablation of individual aggregation methods, and alternative text-centric model (traditional semantic text encoder)
COST: 360 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Late interaction aggregation outperforms the other two methods, but may run too long to be practical; element-wise addition is the fastest, but most likely over-simplifies the signal combination.

ACTION: ADD 2
TITLE: Real-World Validation of Aggregation Methods
PROPOSAL: Evaluate the aggregation methods from proposal 1 on the visual document retrieval benchmark (e.g. VDC, Visual Document Corpus). Specifically, compare the ranking metrics (Recall@10, Precision@1) of the aggregation methods when using the output embeddings from the baseline multimodal retriever (ColPali-based encoder) and the lightweight dense text retriever (as proposed in the problem statement).
CONTROLS: Baseline multimodal retriever, lightweight dense text retriever, and aggregation methods (element-wise addition, fusion with neural attention, late interaction)
COST: 750 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: A combination of the dense text retriever and vision-centric model with late interaction aggregation may show an absolute improvement in Recall@10 and Precision@1 over the baseline. However, a recall "floor" induced by the essential modality gap persists.

ACTION: ADD 3
TITLE: Reducing Latency with Approximate Methods
PROPOSAL: Investigate methods to speed up late interaction aggregation: a) approximate K-nearest neighbors search (k-NN) in embedding space for initial document short-listing, followed by refinement with exact late interaction aggregation; b) simplification of the late interaction neural networks (e.g. by pruning, weight sharing); and c) approximate embedding quantization. Evaluate their trade-offs between precision and latency in comparison to exact late interaction aggregation.
CONTROLS: Baseline multimodal retriever, aggregation methods (element-wise addition, fusion with neural attention), and approximate methods (approximate k-NN, simplified neural networks, approximate embedding quantization)
COST: 540 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Approximate k-NN or approximate embedding quantization may significantly reduce average query latency, but with a decrease in ranking precision which may be tolerable given the large scale of the document collections.

ACTION: REVISE 3
TITLE: REVISED Reducing Latency with Approximate Methods
PROPOSAL: Investigate methods to speed up late interaction aggregation by a) approximate K-nearest neighbors search (k-NN) in embedding space for initial document short-listing, followed by refinement with exact late interaction aggregation; and b) uniform sampling of a fraction of the neural network weights during training to enable fast parallelization and compression of the late interaction neural networks. Evaluate their trade-offs between precision and latency in comparison to exact late interaction aggregation.
CONTROLS: Baseline multimodal retriever, aggregation methods (element-wise addition, fusion with neural attention), and approximate methods (approximate k-NN, sampled neural networks)
COST: 900 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Uniform sampling of neural network weights and approximate k-NN may be more effective for reducing latency while maintaining ranking precision than the alternative methods investigated.

ACTION: ADD 4
TITLE: Complementary Aspects of Text and Vision
PROPOSAL: Examine how the dense text retriever and vision-centric model capture complementary aspects of the documents by visualizing their feature spaces using techniques such as t-SNE, PCA, and UMAP. Investigate how these aspects relate to performance on the retrieval task, aiming to understand the strengths and limitations of each model.
CONTROLS: Baseline multimodal retriever, lightweight dense text retriever, and visualization techniques (t-SNE, PCA, UMAP)
COST: 1215.6 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Visualization of the feature spaces will reveal clusters of semantically similar documents that are better captured by one model or the other, and that this modality-specific capture of different aspects contributes to hybrid retrieval performance. However, reliably predicting which aspect each document will capture based on characteristics such as text and image properties may prove challenging.

ACTION: ADD 5
TITLE: Supervised Weight Transfer for Hybrid Retrievers
PROPOSAL: Propose a method for supervised weight transfer to improve the performance of the lightweight dense text retriever used in the hybrid retriever. This will be achieved by fine-tuning the dense text retriever on the outputs of the vision-centric model (ColPali-based encoder) while keeping the weights of the vision-centric model frozen. Evaluate the transfer learning benefits in terms of retrieval effectiveness and latency.
CONTROLS: Baseline multimodal retriever, aggregation methods (element-wise addition, fusion with neural attention), and fine-tuning approach
COST: 560.5 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Weight transfer under supervision improves performance of the lightweight text retriever, enabling hybrid retrieval to approach or even surpass the baseline vision-centric retriever, assuming that a correct modality-weight is associated with each hybrid score during training of the hyper-binary logistic leaning transfer methods.

ACTION: ADD 6
TITLE: Efficient Indexing for Hybrid Retrievers
PROPOSAL: Investigate efficient indexing strategies to store the outputs of both models, allowing for faster retrieval and aggregation at query time. Study the trade-offs between indexing dimensionality, sparsity, and quantization quality for memory usage, query time, and retrieval performance on the hybrid retriever output.
CONTROLS: Baseline hybrid retriever, indexing methods (dimensionality reduction, sparse factorization, quantization), and approximation error bounds
COST: 1560 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: By carefully optimizing the indexing techniques and parameters (e.g., dimensionality reduction ratio, index sparsity level), memory consumption and query time can be significantly reduced, making it more practical and scalable for the deployment of hybrid retrievers in real-world scenarios.

ACTION: ADD 7
TITLE: Adversarial Training for Hybrid Retrieval
